name: Belize
summary: A blue field with narrow red stripes at top and bottom and a large white disc holding the coat of arms: two woodcutters beside a shield, under a mahogany tree, with the motto 'Sub Umbra Floreo'. It has twelve colours, more than any other national flag.
origin: Before independence, British Honduras used a blue flag with the arms in a white disc, adopted in 1950, which became a symbol of the independence movement. The red stripes were added at independence on 21 September 1981.

symbols.name: Two woodcutters
symbols.description: A Mestizo man holding an axe and a Creole man holding a paddle, flanking the shield.
symbols.meaning: The logwood and mahogany trade that founded the colony, and the country's diverse people.

symbols.name: Mahogany tree
symbols.meaning: The timber industry; the motto 'Sub Umbra Floreo' means 'Under the shade I flourish'.

symbols.name: Wreath of 50 leaves
symbols.description: A green wreath around the arms.
symbols.meaning: 1950, the year the independence movement began.

history.label: British Honduras
history.note: Unofficial flag without the red stripes.

facts: It is the only national flag to depict human beings as a main element.
With twelve colours, it has more than any other national flag.
Belize is the only Central American country with English as the official language.
clues: Blue with red edge stripes and two men flanking a shield under a tree in a white disc.
The only national flag depicting people as its main element.
Its motto means 'Under the shade I flourish'.
